title: Relaxation of Locus Standi — Pro Bono Publico Standing

content.overview: PIL relaxes traditional locus standi so a bona fide petitioner may approach constitutional courts for public injury or for persons unable to litigate effectively. Standing is liberalised, not abolished; busybodies and private disputes fail.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Public or class injury? (2) Bona fide petitioner? (3) Affected class unable to approach? (4) Private gain? (5) Forum 32 or 226?
content.study:
Core rule: Strict personal injury standing shut out the poor. Courts recognised pro bono publico standing for genuine public-interest claims under Articles 32 and 226.

Aligned with companion thin topic locus-standi. Bona fides, substantial public injury, and absence of personal gain remain essential. Abuse guidelines and costs apply.

Case-law verification remains separate.

sections.heading: Traditional standing problem
sections.body: Personal legal injury requirements excluded classes without means or voice.

sections.heading: Pro bono publico standing
sections.body: Bona fide petitioner may be heard for public injury or for others who cannot approach effectively.

sections.heading: Bona fides and public injury
sections.body: Genuineness of purpose and substantial public character of the claim are required.

sections.heading: What standing is not
sections.body: Not a free pass for busybodies, publicity-seekers, or private rivalries labelled as PIL.

sections.heading: Forum
sections.body: Standing operates within Article 32 or 226; it does not create a new court.

examples.title: Representative claim
examples.body: Organisation approaches for bonded labourers who cannot litigate — classic liberal standing if bona fide.

examples.title: Busybody
examples.body: Petitioner with no genuine concern seeks political advantage — standing fails.

hypotheticals.question: Does liberal standing mean anyone may sue for anything?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Public injury and bona fides remain essential; private disputes fail.

distinctions.title: Locus standi vs epistolary practice
distinctions.right: How a matter may be started (letter as petition).

misconceptions.trap: Liberal standing abolished all standing rules.
misconceptions.correction: Standing was relaxed for bona fide public interest; filters remain.

cases.name: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India
cases.issue: When may a person approach for public injury?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Standing may be relaxed where the directly affected cannot approach effectively and the petitioner acts bona fide.

cases.ratioDecidendi: Flexible procedure for effective rights enforcement.
